review.summary: approve_with_nits. The generator is sound and the diff only adds lines; no content lost. Note: the shell was unavailable in this session, so I could not run make_toc --check, check_links or pytest myself; findings come from reading the code and diff. Top three: (1) Week 2 review contents line shows two links both labelled "Exercise" because label() matches the shorter SHORT key first; (2) make_toc.py ships with no test and CI does not run --check, so a stale list is only caught if a reviewer remembers; (3) compiled .pyc files are committed and there is no .gitignore.

findings.checklist_item: Contents list: generated labels must tell sections apart
findings.title: Week 2 review contents line has two links both labelled "Exercise"
findings.claim: The Week 2 review line reads "[Exercise](#integrative-exercise) · [Exercise](#integrative-exercise--worked-answer)": the exercise and its worked answer get the same label, so a phone reader cannot tell which to tap. Cause: label() (tools/make_toc.py:58-60) walks SHORT in insertion order and returns on the first key that is a prefix, so "integrative exercise — worked answer" matches "integrative exercise" before any answer mapping is considered.
findings.evidence: Diff, weeks/week-02-core-mechanics.md line 19: "[Exercise](#integrative-exercise) · [Exercise](#integrative-exercise--worked-answer)". tools/make_toc.py:58-60: `for k, v in SHORT.items(): if key.startswith(k + " ") ...: return v`. Heading at weeks/week-02-core-mechanics.md:1024 is "### Integrative exercise — worked answer".
findings.proposed_change: Add an explicit entry "integrative exercise — worked answer": "Exercise answer" to SHORT (or match the longest key first and treat any key containing "answer" as the answer label), re-run `python3 tools/make_toc.py`, and confirm the Week 2 line reads "[Exercise](#integrative-exercise) · [Exercise answer](#integrative-exercise--worked-answer)". Add this case to the label test proposed in F2.

findings.checklist_item: E. Repo and tooling: a change to tools/ scripts comes with a test or a reason
findings.title: New tools/make_toc.py has no test; idempotency and round-trip are only asserted in the PR text
findings.claim: The PR says the script is idempotent and that stripping the generated lines returns the original files exactly, but tests/ contains only review-harness tests (test_review_contract.py, test_review_harness.py). Nothing in the repo will catch a future regression in strip_generated/build (for example a change to the blank-line handling that makes --check flap, or an anchor-numbering change that diverges from check_links.py).
findings.evidence: Glob tests/**/*.py returns only tests/test_review_contract.py and tests/test_review_harness.py. PR description: "checked: removing the generated lines gives back the original files exactly" (manual, not committed).
findings.proposed_change: Add tests/test_make_toc.py with: (a) build(build(x)) == build(x) and "".join(strip_generated(build(x).splitlines(True))) == x on a small fixture week file; (b) label() cases including "Sources (the week's anchors)", "Integrative exercise — `run_site`, week-3 edition" and "Integrative exercise — worked answer"; (c) anchors from headings() equal check_links.slug with the same -1/-2 numbering for a duplicate heading; (d) every real weeks/*.md is unchanged by build() (the --check invariant). Run `PYTHONPATH=scripts python -m pytest -q tests`.

findings.checklist_item: E. Repo and tooling: each week's contents list is current (--check)
findings.title: CI does not run make_toc.py --check, so a stale contents list only fails if a reviewer remembers
findings.claim: STYLE.md now says `--check` fails when a list is out of date and REVIEW.md asks the reviewer to run it, but checks.yml runs only check_links.py and pytest. The PR text says the Saturday update runs the script before opening its PR, but that task is not in the repo, so the only enforcement is manual. A weekly PR that adds a lesson without re-running the script would merge with a contents list missing that lesson.
findings.evidence: .github/workflows/checks.yml:20-23 has steps for `python3 tools/check_links.py .` and `PYTHONPATH=scripts python -m pytest -q tests` only. STYLE.md:58: "`python3 tools/make_toc.py --check` fails if a list is out of date."
findings.proposed_change: Add a step to checks.yml: `- name: Contents lists\n  run: python3 tools/make_toc.py --check`. Test by pushing a branch with one heading renamed and no regeneration; the job must fail with "contents out of date: weeks/...".

findings.title: Compiled bytecode is committed: new tools/__pycache__ file and a modified scripts/review_harness pyc
findings.claim: The PR adds tools/__pycache__/make_toc.cpython-313.pyc and changes scripts/review_harness/__pycache__/respond.cpython-313.pyc. The repo has no .gitignore, so every local run of a tool or the tests will keep producing binary diffs in PRs, and the pyc for Python 3.13 is useless to the CI runner on 3.12.
findings.evidence: Diff: "new file mode 100644 ... Binary files /dev/null and b/tools/__pycache__/make_toc.cpython-313.pyc differ" and "Binary files a/scripts/review_harness/__pycache__/respond.cpython-313.pyc and b/... differ". Glob for .gitignore found no file. checks.yml:16 pins python-version 3.12.
findings.proposed_change: Add a .gitignore with `__pycache__/` and `*.pyc`, run `git rm -r --cached tools/__pycache__ scripts/review_harness/__pycache__`, and commit. Verify with `git status --short` after running the tests: no pyc files should appear.

findings.checklist_item: E. Repo and tooling: tools/ scripts do what they claim
findings.title: A missing <!-- /toc --> marker makes make_toc.py drop the rest of the file and write it back
findings.claim: strip_generated sets skip=True at START and only clears it at END. If END is ever deleted (a hand edit, or a model rewriting the top of a week file), every later line is skipped, build() rebuilds the file as title plus an empty contents list, and main() overwrites the file in non-check mode. The PR's own evidence (round-trip equality) only covers well-formed input.
findings.evidence: tools/make_toc.py:72-79: `if s == START: skip = True ... if s == END: skip = False ... if skip: continue`; no check after the loop that skip is False. main() (lines 148-162) writes `new` whenever `new != old`.
findings.proposed_change: After the loop in strip_generated, raise SystemExit naming the file when skip is still True, and refuse to write when the rebuilt body is much shorter than the input. Add a test that a file with START but no END raises rather than returning a truncated list.

findings.title: make_toc.py and check_links.py each carry their own slug and fence logic; they can drift apart
findings.claim: make_toc.slug first strips markdown link syntax before slugging; check_links.slug does not. Both toggle code fences only on lines that start with ``` at column 0 (the indented fence at weeks/week-02-core-mechanics.md:586 is ignored by both, harmlessly) and neither handles ~~~. Today the two agree on every heading, but a heading with a link or a tilde fence would make `--check` pass while check_links reports NOANCHOR, or the reverse.
findings.evidence: tools/make_toc.py:46-50 vs tools/check_links.py:4-7; fence handling at make_toc.py:91-95 and check_links.py:14-15.
findings.proposed_change: Move slug() and the fence-aware heading scanner into one small shared module imported by both scripts, so parity is by construction; cover it with the anchor test from F2.

findings.title: RESPOND.md rule 6 does not tell the author to regenerate the contents lists
findings.claim: An author response that adds or renames a heading will leave the generated list stale. Rule 6 names check_links.py and pytest only; rule 1 points to STYLE.md, which does say to run make_toc.py, but the end-of-run checklist is where it will actually be remembered.
findings.evidence: review/RESPOND.md, "Rules for changes" item 6: "Run `python3 tools/check_links.py .` (it must report `bad 0`) and `python -m pytest -q tests` at the end". STYLE.md:58 adds the make_toc requirement separately.
findings.proposed_change: Extend rule 6: "Run `python3 tools/make_toc.py` if you added or renamed any heading, then `python3 tools/make_toc.py --check`, `python3 tools/check_links.py .` (bad 0) and `python -m pytest -q tests`." If F3 lands, CI backs this up.

findings.checklist_item: Lesson template: review days become a Week N review section with the integrative exercise and its answer
findings.title: Contents lists expose inconsistent review-section headings across weeks (pre-existing, now visible)
findings.claim: The integrative answer is headed "Worked answer" in weeks 1, 3 and 4 (label "Answer"), "Integrative answer" in weeks 5 and 6 (label "Exercise answer"), and "Integrative exercise — worked answer" in week 2. The recap is "The week in six paragraphs" in weeks 1, 5 and 6 and "Recap" in 2, 3 and 4. The generator now puts these side by side at the top of every chapter, so the inconsistency reads as different structures. Not introduced by the PR; the PR makes it visible.
findings.evidence: Grep over weeks/: "### Integrative answer" at week-05:947 and week-06:910; "### Worked answer" after "### Integrative exercise" at week-01:909, week-03:1024, week-04:1039; week-02:1024 "### Integrative exercise — worked answer". Contents lines: week-05 line 19 "[Exercise answer](#integrative-answer)" vs week-01 line 19 "[Answer](#worked-answer-6)".
findings.proposed_change: Either settle on one heading pair for every review in a follow-up, updating every anchor link first (glossary.md and reading-list.md may link to #worked-answer-6; run check_links after), or leave headings alone and normalise only the labels in SHORT so all weeks read "Recap · Self-quiz · Exercise · Exercise answer · Sources". The second option needs no anchor changes.

findings.title: STYLE.md says each week file "starts with" the contents list; it starts with the title
findings.claim: "Every week file starts with a generated contents list" is slightly off: the file starts with the `# Week N — ...` title and the list follows it (the script requires the title on line 1, make_toc.py:111-112). README's "How to read this" also does not mention the new lists, which are the main navigation aid on a phone.
findings.evidence: STYLE.md:58; weeks/week-01-what-an-agent-is.md:1-4 (title, blank, `<!-- toc -->`, `## Contents`); tools/make_toc.py:111-112 `if not lines or not lines[0].startswith("# "): return text`.
findings.proposed_change: STYLE.md: "Every week file has a generated contents list right under its title (between ...)". README "How to read this": add one sentence, e.g. "Each chapter opens with a contents list; a ↑ Contents link before each lesson takes you back to it."
